blocks.value: The MBA GM course Full Form is MBA in General Management, a 2-year PG degree course that teaches business administration principles and techniques. It is designed to equip you with broad skills in many aspects of business management. This course covers key areas such as finance, marketing, operations, human resources, and strategic management .

You have to obtain a UG degree in a relevant discipline to get admission to the General Management MBA course in India, followed by entrance exam scores like CAT , XAT, NMAT, CMAT, ATMA , TANCET , etc. Some popular MBA in General Management colleges include PDEU, Vishwa Vishwani Institute of Systems and Management, PIGM Indore, DGVC, etc.

After the course, you can become a General Manager, Project Manager, Business Development Manager, Product Manager, or Human Resources Manager . If interested, you can continue reading the article for more details on MBA General Management course.

blocks.value: Master of Business Administration is a PG degree course that offers advanced management and business training. The course enlightens students with the knowledge and abilities they need to be successful in leadership positions. The growing number of businesses has highlighted the importance of MBA degree.

questions.question_text: Is NMAT mock test released officially?

answers.answer_text: GMAC provides official NMAT mock tests on its website. Two free mock tests, each containing 108 questions with exam structure similar to the actual test is provided online. Candidates can alson pay to purchase NMAT mock tests.

questions.question_text: Will GMAC release NMAT question papers?

answers.answer_text: No. GMAC does not release NMAT question papers. Candidates can find NMAT sample papers issued by different coaching institutes that may have a similar test structure as that of NMAT exam.

questions.question_text: What is the NMAT admit card release date?

answers.answer_text: GMAC does not release NMAT admit card on a specified date for all applicants. NMAT admit card is issued to the candidates based on their scheduled exam date. Candidates can find NMAT Admit card 6-7 days before their exam date.

questions.question_text: How to find NMAT admit card?

answers.answer_text: Candidates can find NMAT admit card inside the login dashboard. GMAC issues NMAT admit card to all candidates who complete the online registration process.

questions.question_text: How difficult is JIPMAT exam compared to IPMAT?

answers.answer_text: Generally, JIPMAT is considered easier than IPMAT Indore and IPMAT Rohtak. Past test-takers have specifically noted that the Quantitative Aptitude and Verbal Ability sections are relatively easy.

questions.question_text: Is it a good idea to give multiple MBA entrance exams like CAT CMAT XAT MAT?
questions.answer_text: Yes, giving multiple MBA entrance exams like CAT, CMAT, XAT, and MAT is generally a good idea. Most of the syllabus overlaps, so your preparation works across exams, and it reduces the risk of depending on just one test.Different exams open doors to different colleges. For example, CAT is needed for IIMs, while exams like CMAT, MAT, or NMAT are accepted by many private B-schools. Colleges such as Athena School of Management also consider multiple exams and focus on the overall profile, so having more scores gives you flexibility.Overall, multiple exams simply mean more options and backup choices, which is always helpful.

questions.question_text: Is quality of MBA education declining?
questions.answer_text: I don't think the quality of MBA education is declining overall, but it's becoming very uneven. A lot more colleges have opened in the last few years, so the quality really depends on the institute you choose.Top and mid-tier B-schools still maintain good faculty, internships and placement support. But some smaller colleges don't update their curriculum or offer enough industry exposure, which makes the experience feel outdated.So it's not that MBA quality is falling everywhere — it's just important to pick a college that focuses on practical learning, internships and industry linkages rather than just classroom teaching.
